title: Basis on Which a Northbeam Returns and Restocking Restocking Fee Is Worked Out
content:
The restocking fee is the schedule's percentage of the price paid on the line, times the units coming back, then raised to the schedule's minimum, cut to the schedule's cap, and rounded to the cent. Where the schedule charges a flat activated device fee, that fee is charged instead of the percentage fee, the two are never charged together, and the schedule's percentage minimum and percentage cap do not bound it, though the fee charged on that branch is never less than nothing. No fee at all is charged where the grade recorded is that the item was defective on arrival or not as described, or where the reason recorded is that the wrong item was shipped, and in that case nothing is charged and the schedule's minimum does not apply. The days the item was held are counted from the day the item was delivered to the day it was booked in. The grade recorded on the fee entry is the condition the inspection recorded for the item, and no other condition is recorded against the fee.

## The percentage fee

The percentage fee on a Northbeam Returns and Restocking return is the schedule's restocking percentage taken on the price paid on the line, times the units coming back.

## The three amounts the clause above distinguishes

Because the third sentence disapplies the schedule's minimum in the case it names, the three amounts stand in this order of precedence.

| Which sentence governs | The fee charged |
| --- | --- |
| the grade recorded is that the item was defective on arrival or not as described, or the reason recorded is that the wrong item was shipped | nothing, and because the schedule's minimum does not apply, the fee charged is 0.00 USD and not the schedule's minimum |
| the schedule charges a flat activated device fee | that flat fee; the schedule's percentage minimum and percentage cap do not bound it, and the fee charged on that branch is never less than nothing |
| neither of the above | the percentage fee, raised to the schedule's minimum and cut to the schedule's cap |

The raising to the minimum, the cutting to the cap and the rounding to the cent are taken last of all.

## Worked through on hypothetical inputs

Take a return on a schedule publishing a restocking percentage of 8 per cent, a minimum of 12.00 USD and a cap of 150.00 USD, and no flat activated device fee.

*Two units at 250.00 USD each.* The price paid on the line times the units coming back is 500.00 USD; the percentage fee at 8 per cent is 40.00 USD; 40.00 USD is above the minimum and below the cap, so the fee charged is 40.00 USD.

*One unit at 60.00 USD.* The percentage fee is 4.80 USD, which is below the minimum, so it is raised to 12.00 USD.

*One unit at 5000.00 USD.* The percentage fee is 400.00 USD, which is above the cap, so it is cut to 150.00 USD.

*The same one unit at 60.00 USD, the grade recorded being that the item was defective on arrival.* Nothing at all is charged, and the schedule's minimum does not apply to it: the fee charged is 0.00 USD, not the 12.00 USD the minimum would otherwise have produced.

*A return on a schedule publishing a flat activated device fee of 40.00 USD.* The fee charged is that flat 40.00 USD, and the percentage minimum of 12.00 USD and percentage cap of 150.00 USD do not bound it; on that branch the fee charged is never less than nothing.

## The two further clauses

The days the item was held are counted from the day the item was delivered to the day it was booked in. The grade recorded on the fee entry is the condition the inspection recorded for the item, and no other condition is recorded against the fee.
